title: Structure analysis
examples: How does the writer make you feel at the beginning of the story?
Can you point out where the writer changes the topic?
Does the ending feel sudden or planned?

explain.say: We are looking at how a writer builds a text.
An opening grabs the reader's attention right away.
A shift in focus moves the reader to a new idea or character.
The ending leaves the reader with a final thought or feeling.
Pace controls how quickly or slowly the story moves along.

draw.text: Pace: Speed of the narrative action.

explain.say: In a play, a sudden change in lighting can signal a shift in focus.

draw.text: Real life: Lighting change signals shift.

faq.q: What is the difference between pace and structure?
faq.a: Structure is the overall plan of the text. Pace is how fast or slow the writing feels while you read it.
asks: Is pace related to the ending?

faq.q: How do I spot a shift in focus when I read?
faq.a: Look for transition words like however or meanwhile. These words signal the writer is moving somewhere new.
asks: Where do I look for a shift?

faq.q: Does every story have a clear opening, middle, and end?
faq.a: Most stories do, but some modern texts might blur these lines. You still look for a beginning, a turning point, and a conclusion.
asks: Can a story skip the opening?
What if the ending is open?

faq.q: If the pace is fast, what is the writer probably doing?
faq.a: The writer is likely using short sentences and action verbs. This keeps the reader moving quickly through the events.
asks: What makes a text feel fast?
How do I show quick action?

faq.q: Can a writer use a shift in focus to confuse the reader?
faq.a: Yes, sometimes writers do this for effect. It can make the reader question what they just read or what is important.
asks: Is changing focus always good writing?

facts: Openings often use vivid imagery to immerse the reader.
A shift in focus can be marked by changes in tense or point of view.
A fast pace uses short, punchy sentences.
Endings can be conclusive, suggesting a clear answer, or ambiguous.

quiz.say: If a writer uses very long descriptions of a room, which element are they controlling?
quiz.why: Long descriptions slow the reader down, which is controlling the pace.

wrong.0: A shift moves to a new thing, it doesn't describe one thing slowly.
wrong.1: The ending is what happens last, not what is happening now.
wrong.3: The opening is just the start; the description happens later.

quiz.say: When a text suddenly changes from talking about a battle to talking about a character's thoughts, what is happening?
quiz.why: This change signals the writer is moving the reader's attention to a new area.

wrong.1: The opening must happen at the very beginning of the text.
wrong.2: Pace relates to speed, not the change of subject.
wrong.3: The ending is the final part of the text.

quiz.say: A text that begins with 'The rain had been falling for three days' is using which structural technique?
quiz.why: This sentence immediately sets the time and atmosphere for the reader.

wrong.0: The opening must occur before the story concludes.
wrong.2: This sentence establishes the main topic, it does not change it.
wrong.3: While it sets the pace, its primary role here is establishing the start.
